terra.problem: The line about a king with a big hat suggests Hezekiah wore one, which the text does not say.
The text does not say Hezekiah consulted his leaders before he did anything.
The text does not say that anyone looking for a drink was surprised.
The text does not say that digging would produce more water or that nobody was given a shovel.
The people aim to prevent the Assyrian kings from finding plenty of water. The text does not say the kings came up dry.
The text does not say Hezekiah built the outer wall because one wall was not enough for him.
An outer wall is not a wall on top of another wall.
The text does not say nobody was counting coins.
The text calls the Assyrian army vast but does not establish whether Judah's army was bigger or smaller.
Calling Sennacherib an angry guy assigns him a feeling the text does not give.
Adding the LORD to the pile of gods Sennacherib has beaten suggests he has defeated the LORD. Sennacherib only claims the LORD cannot deliver His people.
Sennacherib claims those gods could not deliver their people. He does not claim that none held him off for a while.
The claim that Sennacherib would never admit to losing a battle goes beyond what the text says.
The text does not say Sennacherib wrote letters because speeches were not enough for him.
The passage says Sennacherib's servants spoke against the LORD and that Sennacherib wrote letters. It does not say he personally mocked the LORD out loud.
The text gives the purpose of the shouting, but does not say they chose Hebrew so every word would land.
The claim that the LORD made everything comes from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The claim that hail appears in other Bible stories needs a reference.
Hezekiah being exalted in the eyes of all nations does not establish that nobody looked down on him.
